goalDecisions.goal: Describe solids, liquids and gases using arrangement, movement and energy.
goalDecisions.judgement: The particle/energy model distinguishes arrangement, motion and attractive forces with original picture-reading/correction tasks.

goalDecisions.goal: Explain a change of state without claiming the particles themselves melt.
goalDecisions.judgement: State-change explanations conserve the particles themselves and distinguish heating/cooling and energy transfer from particles melting.

goalDecisions.goal: Interpret solubility data using mass of solvent rather than solution.
goalDecisions.judgement: Mass-of-solvent denominator, curves, saturation and residue/error calculations are explicitly taught and assessed with Paper2C scope.

goalDecisions.goal: Choose separation methods from the properties of a mixture.
goalDecisions.judgement: Mixture/property differences select the separation route and distinguish recovery, purity and chemical change.

goalDecisions.goal: Calculate and interpret chromatographic Rf values under stated conditions.
goalDecisions.judgement: Actual distance ratios, matched conditions and limited identification from one chromatogram support both calculation and interpretation.

goalDecisions.goal: Calculate particle counts and relative atomic mass from isotope data.
goalDecisions.judgement: Nuclear/charge counts and weighted abundance calculations use explicit denominators and original independent quantities.

goalDecisions.goal: Use electronic configuration to explain main-group positions.
goalDecisions.judgement: All first20 configurations and main-group/period/shell contrasts distinguish similar outer shells from identical total electrons.

goalDecisions.goal: Explain ionic, covalent and metallic bonding using electrostatic attraction.
goalDecisions.judgement: Electrostatic attraction is identified in each bonding model with correct nuclei/shared-pair/mobile-electron roles and Paper2C metallic scope.

goalDecisions.goal: Draw and check electron-transfer and shared-electron representations.
goalDecisions.judgement: Original displayed electron models, local valency and whole-model counts cover required ionic and molecular representations rather than copied simplified names alone.

goalDecisions.goal: Connect structure and charge-carrier mobility to physical properties.
goalDecisions.judgement: Network/molecular/metallic comparisons distinguish the relevant attraction and mobile-charge mechanism without saying ordinary boiling breaks molecular covalent bonds.

goalDecisions.goal: Connect amount, mass and equation ratios, and calculate yield and formulae from evidence.
goalDecisions.judgement: Original limiting-amount, yield, formula and experimental-mass tasks independently preserve units, conservation and assumptions.

goalDecisions.goal: Use solution and gas-volume calculations with exact units and Paper2C applicability.
goalDecisions.judgement: Paper2C solution/gas amounts require explicit dm3/cm3 conversion and the specified rtp molar-volume basis.

goalDecisions.goal: Explain charge carriers, predict molten/aqueous electrolysis products and balance half-equations for Paper 2C.
goalDecisions.judgement: Named molten/aqueous cases and transferable atom/charge half-equations distinguish water competition, electrode sign and electron direction.

goalDecisions.goal: Evaluate electrolysis observations without treating graphite as universally inert.
goalDecisions.judgement: Investigation controls and active/inert electrode contrasts reject universal graphite inertness and unsupported gas/purity inferences.

goalDecisions.goal: Translate studied and supplied unfamiliar reaction identities into word, balanced formula or structural equations with justified state symbols and representation limits.
goalDecisions.judgement: The source-constrained studied collection and fully supplied unfamiliar tasks combine names, coefficients, phases and structural/physical representation limits;69modelrecords alone are not used as proof.

prerequisiteReview.judgement: The particle/model prerequisite is stated; chemical vocabulary, charges, formulas, amount and unit procedures are developed within the chapter with worked examples. Elementary arithmetic/reading are appropriate course-entry skills, not assumed advanced chemistry.

coherenceReview.judgement: Core particle/atom/structure methods precede quantitative and electrolysis topics; original evidence/correction sections deepen each skill. The later named/family reaction reference explicitly supports cross-topic1.25 and preserves C-only labels, structural versus molecular limits and supplied-state assumptions. Search and contents provide direct access; completion concerns authored coverage, not an imposed linear learner mastery claim.
